requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
Almost every obligation is implemented and tested. One gap remains: `habeas author --stdout` never warns, although the text says `habeas author` MUST warn after it finishes.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **`habeas status` warns about every item without recent coverage.**
  - Code: `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]` calls `inspected_coverage_warnings`, then `coverage_warnings` in `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]`.
  - The status section is `coverage_section`; the warnings are not filtered by the status selection or `--all`.
  - Tests:
    - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]`
    - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]`, which covers the `reauthored`, `new_function` and `test_module` examples.
- **`habeas author` warns after it finishes.**
  - Code: `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]`, called from the `--all` and sites batch path, the "current record kept" path, and the single-subject file path.
  - Tests: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_coverage_warnings_on_stderr]`, the `tests/authoring_batch.rs` tests, and `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject`.
- **Each warning names file, line, kind and name.**
  - Code: `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[uncovered_error]` builds "file:line: kind name has no recent coverage…", and `UncoveredItem` carries it.
  - Tests assert strings of that form, such as "function render has no recent coverage" preceded by the file and line.
- **Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.**
  - Code: `in_tests_module` (inline `mod tests`) and `in_tests_file` (out-of-line `tests.rs` or `tests/…`) set `in_tests`, and `warnings` filters on it.
  - Tests: `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` (inline `fixture`), `items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about`, and `files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module`.
- **A warning MUST NOT fail validation.**
  - Code: `validate_rust_functions` puts uncovered items in `uncovered`, not in `errors`. Only untested `#[test]` functions become errors, and that obligation belongs to `coverage.tests`.
  - Test: the `validate_repository` assertion at the end of `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item`.
- **Repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.**
  - Code: validation uses only `reads.covers`, the current records. The `git2` history reading is confined to `coverage_history`, which only `warnings` calls.
  - Test: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` removes the Git objects and shows validation results are unchanged.

**Gap**
- In `src/main.rs#fn[main]`, `habeas author <subject> --stdout` skips `print_coverage_warnings` (`if !stdout`). The comment there says the warnings would describe the evidence on disk rather than this record. The command still finishes successfully.
- The requirement says `habeas author` MUST warn when it finishes and makes no exception for `--stdout`.
- The authoring text only requires that diagnostics go to stderr in stdout mode, so warnings could have been printed there.
- `batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones` asserts the omission, so it is a deliberate, unspecified carve-out.
- Reading the requirement as "after any completed author run", this violates a MUST. Reading it as "after authoring writes evidence", the carve-out is fine. The wording supports both readings, and they lead to different conclusions, so this is a gap.
- No `{fixme}` acknowledges it.

Skipping warnings for a cancelled batch is consistent with "after it finishes" and is not a gap.

text: :::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
